title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether a deterministic verifier-guided repair pipeline improves the safety/correctness of LLM-generated vendor-CLI configurations relative to blind repair. Using a preregistered controlled-fault, paired design (hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter, shared controlled-fault candidates), we executed 40 planned confirmatory tasks (one shared source candidate per pair). One pair was unscorable; primary analysis used 39 complete pairs. The baseline (blind repair) achieved 30/39 verifier+simulator passes (76.92%); the guarded (verifier-guided) condition achieved 38/39 passes (97.44%). The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.02148; 95% CI [0.07692, 0.35897]. These confirmatory results show a statistically detectable increase in verifier-validated success under the preregistered controlled-fault bank and execution contract. We report execution accounting, preregistration adherence, and limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, simulator-based safety check) and provide a complete artifact bundle for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to assist network operations by producing device configurations and remediation plans. Prior work demonstrates verifier-interposed generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures can raise verifier pass rates in domains such as IaC and code [10], but cross-domain evidence for vendor-CLI configuration repair and controlled measurement of harmful over-repair remains limited. Motivated by the need for operationally meaningful, preregistered evidence, we ask: Does a deterministic verifier-guided LLM repair pipeline reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered controlled-challenge, paired experiment design and frozen task bank of 40 deterministic vendor-CLI controlled faults; (2) a completed confirmatory execution under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics and exact execution accounting; (3) a confirmatory paired analysis showing a 20.51 percentage-point absolute increase in verifier+simulator pass rate for guarded versus baseline (p=0.02148, 95% CI [0.07692,0.35897]); and (4) a full artifact bundle (raw outputs, verifier traces, execution manifest, analysis files) released with the study.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair and verifier-interposed pipelines have been demonstrated to reduce verifier-detected failures in code and IaC domains and to provide typed diagnostics for repair [10]. Iterative verifier-guided refinement has raised pass@1 rates on Terraform/IaC tasks in recent verifier-first evaluations, though gains depend on verifier design, model, and retry budget [Jouini et al., 2026]. Complementary analyses warn of a verifier tax (increased interaction length and cost) and verifier-exploitation pathologies where optimization toward a proxy verifier can degrade the genuine property of interest [Sah et al., 2026; Gupta, 2026]. Surveys of LLM use in NetOps report stronger evidence for read/diagnostic assistance than for closed-loop configuration change, and they emphasise the need for operational assurance contracts when granting execution authority to models. We position this study as a narrowly scoped, preregistered, controlled-challenge evaluation addressing the cross-domain gap by measuring verifier-guided repair on synthetic vendor-CLI tasks with deterministic fault injection and paired semantics.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration: We preregistered the study (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) before observing confirmatory outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference (guarded − baseline). Adapter and pairing semantics: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics (both conditions receive the same preregistered controlled-fault candidate; exactly one repair opportunity per condition). Baseline: blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed). Guarded: repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the model. Task generation and activation: a deterministic controlled-fault generator produced 40 faulted source candidates (controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 archived). Confirmatory sample: task_count fixed at 40; confirmatory execution used the frozen task manifest; calibration/pilot stages were not pooled with confirmatory data. Execution contract: one initial source-generation call per task (shared), maximum model-call budget 120; actual model used: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version=gpt-5-mini). Note: model_configuration.temperature was null/unset in the archived configuration; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Execution and scoring: a deterministic vendor-CLI verifier plus simulator provided an acceptance predicate; primary success required both verifier pass and simulator-based compliance agreement (to detect verifier↔simulator discordance). Analysis plan: exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent), report discordant counts, absolute risk difference with 95% CI via paired bootstrap percentiles (resamples=10000), sensitivity analyses per preregistration. Missingness and stopping rules: exclude a pair only if both condition executions fail for infrastructure reasons (complete_pair_primary). Any adapter-contract failure mandated stop rather than silent substitution.
sections.results: Execution accounting: 40 controlled-fault pairs were planned; execution completed 78 episodes (39 complete pairs); one pair’s source generation was invalid/unscorable and excluded per preregistered rule. Total hosted-model calls recorded = 118 (below the 120 budget). Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs=39): baseline success = 30/39 (76.92%); guarded success = 38/39 (97.44%). Contingency counts: n_11 (both pass) = 29, n_10 (guarded-only pass) = 9, n_01 (baseline-only pass) = 1, n_00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051282051 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0769230769, 0.35897435897] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Sensitivity and secondary analyses: preregistered exploratory per-fault-class analyses and harmful-overrepair audits were recorded in the artifact bundle; they are labeled exploratory and not used to make confirmatory claims in this paper. No deviations from the preregistered primary analysis were made; all exclusions and the single unscorable pair are documented.
sections.discussion: Under the preregistered controlled-challenge design and the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 shared-candidate semantics, exposing deterministic validator diagnostics to the model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated success on our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank. The paired design isolates the effect of validator diagnostics on a single shared controlled-fault candidate (confirmatory estimand). Interpretational boundaries: (1) this result applies to the preregistered controlled faults, the single LLM (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier+simulator used here; it does not prove general production readiness across vendors, models, or operator policies; (2) the study used synthetic controlled faults to ensure intervention activation — naturalistic activation rates in live NetOps workloads remain an open question; (3) runtime costs and latency (the verifier tax) were instrumented and archived; operational feasibility at scale requires further cost/latency tradeoff studies; (4) verifier↔simulator discordances were handled conservatively by requiring agreement for primary success, but remaining uncertainty about real-world grounding remains. These limitations identify concrete next steps: cross-vendor replication, multi-model evaluation, larger task banks drawn from production incident traces, and integrating uncertainty quantification and calibrated model confidence into the repair loop to reduce verifier-exploitation risk.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, controlled-fault, paired experiment using a hosted verifier-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier-and-simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.5 percentage points; p=0.02148). The study demonstrates that, under controlled and artifact-grounded conditions, validator diagnostics can materially affect repair outcomes. However, external validity is limited: the evidence pertains to synthetic controlled faults, a single model, and a deterministic verifier+simulator; production deployment requires additional cross-vendor, multi-model, and cost/latency evaluations. All raw artifacts, execution manifests, and analysis files are archived in the evidence bundle to support independent verification and follow-on work.

disclosure_statement: This study was preregistered (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) and executed under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter. The single LLM declared for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version=gpt-5-mini). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and is cited here by immutable archive reference; that master prompt contains the autonomy boundary and preregistration instructions. Human roles: a Research Director set the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment design, execution, analysis, and manuscript generation without manual human editing of technical content. The confirmatory experiment used a frozen controlled-fault task bank (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: exactly one source-generation per pair was reused by both conditions; baseline is blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded is repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model_configuration records temperature=null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. All prompts, model calls, verifier traces, raw outputs, execution logs, and analysis artifacts were archived and hash-summarised in the execution manifest; the artifact bundle contains the execution manifest, raw_results.jsonl, provider traces, and analysis files. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule: the run would stop if the adapter contract could not be satisfied; no silent adapter substitution occurred. No human manually rewrote or edited the manuscript text after the autonomy lock; autonomous internal revision and checks were performed as described in the preregistration. The full artifact bundle and provenance manifest are available in the archived evidence package accompanying this submission.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad, naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required verifier AND simulator agreement; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: n=39 complete pairs provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup/fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency not resolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires further study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this study’s controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier designs).
